questions.question: Batholiths are landforms created by:
questions.solution:
__
 
• A Batholith__ is a large body of igneous rock formed beneath the Earth's surface by the intrusion and solidification of magma.
 
• They appear on the surface only after the denudational processes remove the overlying materials. 
 
• These are granitic bodies and are the cooled portion of magma chambers.
 
• Lacoliths are large dome-shaped intrusive bodies with a level base and connected by a pipe-like channel from below. 
 
• Phcaolith is an elongated dome of intrusive igneous rock usually located beneath the crest of an anticline or the trough of a syncline.
 
• The near horizontal bodies of the intrusive igneous rocks are called sill or sheet, depending on the thickness of the material.
 
• The thinner ones are called sheets while the thick horizontal deposits are called sills.​

questions.question: Which of the following diseases has been eradicated worldwide?

 Causative Agent
 
 __
 
• Variola virus
 
 
 
 

 Mode of Acquiring
 
 
 
• Inhaling respiratory droplets from an infected person.
 
• Direct contact with the sores.
 
• Touching contaminated surfaces.
 
 
 
 

 Affects
 Skin cells

• Initially flu-like symptoms- fever, headache, back pain, and vomiting
 
• The appearance of red spots which turn into fluid-filled blisters.
 
• After 8-9 days, scabs form which eventually fall off leaving scars.
 
 
 
 

 
• Edward Jenner__ discovered the vaccine for smallpox.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding disinflation?

options.text: A scenario when inflation is mainly due to inflation of only a few commodities and not of all commodities.
A sudden sharp decrease in prices due to unexpected reasons.
A decrease in the rate of inflation in a specific period.
An overall decrease in prices over a specific period.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A decrease in the rate of inflation in a specific period.​**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disinflation refers** to a slowdown in the pace of price inflation. It is not the same as deflation, which is a decrease in the overall price level of goods and services.
 
• **A decrease in the rate of inflation** in a specific period is called disinflation. It is a situation where the prices of goods and services are still rising but at a slower pace than before. This can be caused by several factors, such as a decrease in the growth of the money supply, an increase in the supply of goods and services, or a decrease in demand for goods and services.

questions.question: In the life cycle of a star, the stage nebula refers to:

options.text: a cloud of dust and hydrogen
the stage when the outer layers expand, cool down and become less bright
the last stage of its life
the outer shell of a star

questions.solution:
__
 
• In the life cycle of a star, the stage nebula refers to a cloud of **dust and hydrogen**__.
 
• The nebula is made up of hydrogen and gases that slowly start to collapse under the force of their own gravity.
 
• The nebula collapses due to gravity, it's size gets smaller and smaller.
 
• As the nebula collapses, the particles will get closer to each other and due to which the friction between the particles will occur and it produces the heat.
 
• This heat then causes an increase in pressure which pushes against gravity slowing the collapse of the star. This pressure continues to increase as the nebula gets smaller and the temperature rises, leading to the next stage of a star's life cycle.

questions.question: There is NO vaccine for which of the following hepatitis viruses?
questions.solution:
__
 
• There is NO vaccine for **Hepatitis C**__ viruses.
 
• It is the disease that causes the inflammation and infection of the liver.
 
• This condition develops after the infection of the Hepatitis C virus.
 
• It can be either acute or chronic.

 
 

 __Hepatitis__ is a __viral infection__ that causes liver inflammation. Hepatitis A and E are acute infections whereas Hepatitis B, C, and D are chronic.
 
 

 Causative Agent
 Hepatitis A virus, Hepatitis B virus, Hepatitis C virus, and Hepatitis D virus
 
 

 Mode of Acquiring
 
 
 
• Through the consumption of contaminated food and water (Hepatitis A).
 
• Through contact with infectious fluids like blood, semen or vaginal secretions (Hepatitis B, C, and D).
 
• Through contaminated water (Hepatitis E).
 
 
 
 

 Affects
 Liver
 
 

 Symptoms
 
 
In the case of chronic infections, the symptoms appear slowly and gradually. The common symptoms of Hepatitis are:

 
 
• Flu-like symptoms
 
• Fatigue
 
• Abdominal pain
 
• Weight loss and loss of appetite
 
• Dark urine and pale stool
 
• Yellow eyes and skin (Signs of jaundice)

questions.question: With regard to kidneys and its functions, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.text: Their basic functional units are called nephrons.
Each nephron has two parts – the glomerulus and the renal tubule
They maintain water balance and expel metabolic waste.
Reptiles have relatively more nephrons than birds.

questions.solution:
__Concept__-

__
 
• The kidneys are two bean-shaped organs in our renal system.
 
• Kidneys comprise a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder, and a urethra.
 
• Kidneys are located on either side of the backbone on the posterior surface.
 
• The kidneys perform many vital functions, including maintaining overall balance fluid, regulating, verifying & filtering minerals from the blood, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **A nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidneys.**__
 
• The main functions of kidneys are to regulate the concentration of water and soluble substance like sodium salts like filtering the blood, reabsorb what is needed, and excrete the rest as urine.
 
• Each nephron is composed of two main structures called glomerulus and renal tubule.
 
• There are about 1000000 nephrons in each human kidney.
 
• __**Reptiles have relatively few nephrons (from 3,000 to 30,000 in lizards), while birds have a great number (around 200,000 in a fowl, twice as many as in a mammal of comparable size).**__
